subject: Novacart contract renewal — throughput proof & proposed alignment

Subject: Novacart contract renewal — throughput proof & proposed alignment

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to get ahead of the renewal timeline and surface a compact plan that addresses the two items you raised: 1) measurable throughput improvements for peak inference windows, and 2) term/commit alignment to support your Q4 campaign.

Quick summary of the proposal attached: throughput_comparison_v3.xlsx (short runbook and numbers), and a draft SOW to move to a blended committed tier for the next 12 months. Key asks from our side: a short bake period (2–4 weeks) where we run parallel traffic on your preview pool so we can validate the latency/throughput uplift, and a single procurement PO to lock the committed capacity.

If that sounds reasonable, can we target a technical validation kickoff this Thursday 11:00am PT? I’ve cc’d Marissa (your renewal lead) and Dylan (our performance eng) to own the validation and the SOW updates.

Thanks —
Maya Srinivasan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
maya.s@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Maya —

Appreciate the proactive plan. The throughput numbers look promising at a glance but we need two things before we commit:
- A short, hands-on validation run with our traffic (we can provide a 48-72h window simulating peak)
- A clear SLA on time-to-first-byte and tail latency at 99th percentile during the validation window

Procurement is flexible on the PO cadence but wants a clear pricing delta if we add extra capacity mid-term. Also cc’ing Ken (CTO) to flag any infra concerns.

Thursday 11:00am PT should work for the kickoff; please send a calendar invite and runbook.

Best,
Lena
Head of Operations — Novacart

Maya / Dylan —

Two quick notes from a renewal play perspective:
1) Pricing: Novacart is very price-sensitive post-Q2 — they mentioned rival pricing in our last call. Recommend we include a 6-month option to add burst capacity at a pre-agreed uplift (e.g., +18%) rather than a flat "add-on" negotiation later.
2) Technical validation checklist: Dylan, can your team prepare a short validation script that stresses KV cache churn and long-context hits? Their traffic is heavy on chat personalization so tail p99 is what they care about.

I’ll draft a one-pager save plan (commercial + operational commitments) to attach to SOW.

Subject: RE: Novacart contract renewal — throughput proof & proposed alignment

Lena / Team —

Thanks for the validation window — we ran a simulated 72h preview in our staging cluster against a replay of Novacart peak traffic. High-level results (also attached in throughput_comparison_v3.xlsx):
- Average throughput improvement: ~28% at matched cost, due to smarter KV caching and adjusted batch sizing.
- 99th percentile latency: improved from 840ms -> 570ms for 1024-token requests under peak.
- Edge-case: requests with very long contexts (>8k tokens) saw p99 regressions in one micro-pattern; we isolated it to the attention-split path and have a fix queued for canary.

Operational commitments we propose for the next 12 months:
- 24/7 on-call during Q4 peak windows for the first renewal year (covered in SOW).
- Two scheduled performance reviews per quarter + a pooled credit for three emergency support incidents.

Lena — can you confirm the dates for the 72h replay you’ll provide so we can finalize graphs for the SOW?

Dylan Brooks
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: throughput_comparison_v3.xlsx; runbook-deployment-sla.docx

Thanks for the quick validation window. Based on the staging run and Dylan’s notes, attached is an updated SOW that includes:
- The 72h validation run details and pass/fail criteria
- SLA commitments focused on p50/p95/p99 latency and an escalation ladder
- A commercial clause for mid-term capacity expansion: pre-negotiated uplift tiers (12%, 18%, 25% depending on increment).

Action items:

I’ll follow up with a DocuSign link once procurement confirms the preferred cadence.

Best,
Maya

Thanks for the detailed SOW. We can provide a replay window starting next Tuesday (2028-07-17 00:00 UTC) for the 72h validation. Procurement prefers option B (12-month blended with a 6-month review) provided the mid-term uplift tiers are fixed up front — that looks sane.
